37:   /** number of bits used for quantizing latitude and longitude values */
38:   public static final short BITS = 32;
39: 
40:   private static final double LAT_SCALE = (0x1L << BITS) / 180.0D;
41:   private static final double LAT_DECODE = 1 / LAT_SCALE;
42:   private static final double LON_SCALE = (0x1L << BITS) / 360.0D;
43:   private static final double LON_DECODE = 1 / LON_SCALE;

51:   /**
52:    * Quantizes double (64 bit) latitude into 32 bits (rounding down: in the direction of -90)
53:    *
54:    * @param latitude latitude value: must be within standard +/-90 coordinate bounds.
55:    * @return encoded value as a 32-bit {@code int}
56:    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if latitude is out of bounds
57:    */
58:   public static int encodeLatitude(double latitude) {
59:     checkLatitude(latitude);
60:     // the maximum possible value cannot be encoded without overflow
61:     if (latitude == 90.0D) {
62:       latitude = Math.nextDown(latitude);
63:     }
64:     return (int) Math.floor(latitude / LAT_DECODE);
65:   }

67:   /**
68:    * Quantizes double (64 bit) latitude into 32 bits (rounding up: in the direction of +90)

70:    * @param latitude latitude value: must be within standard +/-90 coordinate bounds.
71:    * @return encoded value as a 32-bit {@code int}
72:    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if latitude is out of bounds
73:    */

75:     GeoUtils.checkLatitude(latitude);
76:     // the maximum possible value cannot be encoded without overflow
77:     if (latitude == 90.0D) {
78:       latitude = Math.nextDown(latitude);
79:     }
80:     return (int) Math.ceil(latitude / LAT_DECODE);
81:   }

84:    * Quantizes double (64 bit) longitude into 32 bits (rounding down: in the direction of -180)

87:    * @return encoded value as a 32-bit {@code int}
88:    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if longitude is out of bounds
89:    */

193:         subBoxes.lonBase,
194:         subBoxes.maxLatDelta,

198:         lon,

206:    * @lucene.internal

210:         box -> tree.relate(box.minLon, box.maxLon, box.minLat, box.maxLat);
211:     final Grid subBoxes =
212:         createSubBoxes(
213:             tree.getMinY(), tree.getMaxY(), tree.getMinX(), tree.getMaxX(), boxToRelation);
214: 
215:     return new Component2DPredicate(
216:         subBoxes.latShift,
217:         subBoxes.lonShift,
218:         subBoxes.latBase,
219:         subBoxes.lonBase,
220:         subBoxes.maxLatDelta,
221:         subBoxes.maxLonDelta,

226:   private static Grid createSubBoxes(
227:       double shapeMinLat,
228:       double shapeMaxLat,
229:       double shapeMinLon,
230:       double shapeMaxLon,
231:       Function<Rectangle, Relation> boxToRelation) {
232:     final int minLat = encodeLatitudeCeil(shapeMinLat);
233:     final int maxLat = encodeLatitude(shapeMaxLat);
234:     final int minLon = encodeLongitudeCeil(shapeMinLon);
235:     final int maxLon = encodeLongitude(shapeMaxLon);
236: 
237:     if (maxLat < minLat || (shapeMaxLon >= shapeMinLon && maxLon < minLon)) {
238:       // the box cannot match any quantized point
239:       return new Grid(1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, new byte[0]);
240:     }
241: 
242:     final int latShift, lonShift;
243:     final int latBase, lonBase;
244:     final int maxLatDelta, maxLonDelta;
245:     {
246:       long minLat2 = (long) minLat - Integer.MIN_VALUE;
247:       long maxLat2 = (long) maxLat - Integer.MIN_VALUE;
248:       latShift = computeShift(minLat2, maxLat2);
249:       latBase = (int) (minLat2 >>> latShift);
250:       maxLatDelta = (int) (maxLat2 >>> latShift) - latBase + 1;
251:       assert maxLatDelta > 0;
252:     }
253:     {
254:       long minLon2 = (long) minLon - Integer.MIN_VALUE;
255:       long maxLon2 = (long) maxLon - Integer.MIN_VALUE;
256:       if (shapeMaxLon < shapeMinLon) { // crosses dateline
257:         maxLon2 += 1L << 32; // wrap
258:       }
259:       lonShift = computeShift(minLon2, maxLon2);
260:       lonBase = (int) (minLon2 >>> lonShift);
261:       maxLonDelta = (int) (maxLon2 >>> lonShift) - lonBase + 1;
262:       assert maxLonDelta > 0;
263:     }
264: 
265:     final byte[] relations = new byte[maxLatDelta * maxLonDelta];
266:     for (int i = 0; i < maxLatDelta; ++i) {
267:       for (int j = 0; j < maxLonDelta; ++j) {
268:         final int boxMinLat = ((latBase + i) << latShift) + Integer.MIN_VALUE;
269:         final int boxMinLon = ((lonBase + j) << lonShift) + Integer.MIN_VALUE;
270:         final int boxMaxLat = boxMinLat + (1 << latShift) - 1;
271:         final int boxMaxLon = boxMinLon + (1 << lonShift) - 1;
272: 
273:         relations[i * maxLonDelta + j] =
274:             (byte)
275:                 boxToRelation
276:                     .apply(
277:                         new Rectangle(
278:                             decodeLatitude(boxMinLat), decodeLatitude(boxMaxLat),
279:                             decodeLongitude(boxMinLon), decodeLongitude(boxMaxLon)))
280:                     .ordinal();
281:       }
282:     }
283: 
284:     return new Grid(latShift, lonShift, latBase, lonBase, maxLatDelta, maxLonDelta, relations);
285:   }

287:   /**
288:    * Compute the minimum shift value so that {@code (b>>>shift)-(a>>>shift)} is less that {@code
289:    * ARITY}.
290:    */
291:   private static int computeShift(long a, long b) {
292:     assert a <= b;
293:     // We enforce a shift of at least 1 so that when we work with unsigned ints
294:     // by doing (lat - MIN_VALUE), the result of the shift (lat - MIN_VALUE) >>> shift
295:     // can be used for comparisons without particular care: the sign bit has
296:     // been cleared so comparisons work the same for signed and unsigned ints
297:     for (int shift = 1; ; ++shift) {
298:       final long delta = (b >>> shift) - (a >>> shift);
299:       if (delta >= 0 && delta < Grid.ARITY) {
300:         return shift;
301:       }
302:     }
303:   }

305:   private static class Grid {
306:     static final int ARITY = 64;
307: 
308:     final int latShift, lonShift;
309:     final int latBase, lonBase;
310:     final int maxLatDelta, maxLonDelta;
311:     final byte[] relations;
312: 
313:     private Grid(
314:         int latShift,
315:         int lonShift,
316:         int latBase,
317:         int lonBase,
318:         int maxLatDelta,
319:         int maxLonDelta,
320:         byte[] relations) {
321:       if (latShift < 1 || latShift > 31) {
322:         throw new IllegalArgumentException();
323:       }
324:       if (lonShift < 1 || lonShift > 31) {
325:         throw new IllegalArgumentException();
326:       }
327:       this.latShift = latShift;
328:       this.lonShift = lonShift;
329:       this.latBase = latBase;
330:       this.lonBase = lonBase;
331:       this.maxLatDelta = maxLatDelta;
332:       this.maxLonDelta = maxLonDelta;
333:       this.relations = relations;

337:   /** A predicate that checks whether a given point is within a distance of another point. */
338:   public static class DistancePredicate extends Grid {
339: 
340:     private final double lat, lon;
341:     private final double distanceKey;
342: 
343:     private DistancePredicate(
344:         int latShift,
345:         int lonShift,
346:         int latBase,
347:         int lonBase,
348:         int maxLatDelta,
349:         int maxLonDelta,
350:         byte[] relations,
351:         double lat,
352:         double lon,
353:         double distanceKey) {
354:       super(latShift, lonShift, latBase, lonBase, maxLatDelta, maxLonDelta, relations);
355:       this.lat = lat;
356:       this.lon = lon;
357:       this.distanceKey = distanceKey;
358:     }

360:     /**
361:      * Check whether the given point is within a distance of another point. NOTE: this operates
362:      * directly on the encoded representation of points.
363:      */
364:     public boolean test(int lat, int lon) {
365:       final int lat2 = ((lat - Integer.MIN_VALUE) >>> latShift);
366:       if (lat2 < latBase || lat2 >= latBase + maxLatDelta) {
367:         return false;
368:       }
369:       int lon2 = ((lon - Integer.MIN_VALUE) >>> lonShift);
370:       if (lon2 < lonBase) { // wrap
371:         lon2 += 1 << (32 - lonShift);
372:       }
373:       assert Integer.toUnsignedLong(lon2) >= lonBase;
374:       assert lon2 - lonBase >= 0;
375:       if (lon2 - lonBase >= maxLonDelta) {
376:         return false;
377:       }
378: 
379:       final int relation = relations[(lat2 - latBase) * maxLonDelta + (lon2 - lonBase)];
380:       if (relation == Relation.CELL_CROSSES_QUERY.ordinal()) {
381:         return SloppyMath.haversinSortKey(
382:                 decodeLatitude(lat), decodeLongitude(lon), this.lat, this.lon)
383:             <= distanceKey;
384:       } else {
385:         return relation == Relation.CELL_INSIDE_QUERY.ordinal();
386:       }

391:   public static class Component2DPredicate extends Grid {

393:     private final Component2D tree;
394:

396:         int latShift,
397:         int lonShift,
398:         int latBase,
399:         int lonBase,
400:         int maxLatDelta,
401:         int maxLonDelta,
402:         byte[] relations,
403:         Component2D tree) {
404:       super(latShift, lonShift, latBase, lonBase, maxLatDelta, maxLonDelta, relations);
405:       this.tree = tree;
406:     }

408:     /**
409:      * Check whether the given point is within the considered polygon. NOTE: this operates directly
410:      * on the encoded representation of points.
411:      */
412:     public boolean test(int lat, int lon) {
413:       final int lat2 = ((lat - Integer.MIN_VALUE) >>> latShift);
414:       if (lat2 < latBase || lat2 >= latBase + maxLatDelta) {
415:         return false;
416:       }
417:       int lon2 = ((lon - Integer.MIN_VALUE) >>> lonShift);
418:       if (lon2 < lonBase) { // wrap
419:         final int wrapDelta = 1 << (32 - lonShift);
420:         lon2 += wrapDelta;
421:       }
422:       assert Integer.toUnsignedLong(lon2) >= lonBase;
423:       assert lon2 - lonBase >= 0;
424:       if (lon2 - lonBase >= maxLonDelta) {
425:         return false;
426:       }
427: 
428:       final int latOffset = lat2 - latBase;
429:       final int lonOffset = lon2 - lonBase;
430:       final int cellIndex = latOffset * maxLonDelta + lonOffset;
431:       final int insideRelation = Relation.CELL_INSIDE_QUERY.ordinal();
432:       final int crossesRelation = Relation.CELL_CROSSES_QUERY.ordinal();
433:       final int relation = relations[cellIndex];

436:         final int encodedLon = lon;
437:         final double latDecode = LAT_DECODE;
438:         final double lonDecode = LON_DECODE;

458:               if (southOk) {

While checking the latitude bounds we are doing the following `lat2 >= latBase + maxLatDelta` which can overflow. On the other hand when checking the longitude we are doing `lon2 - lonBase >= maxLonDelta`. This explain why we are seeing an issue for big latitudes but not for big longitudes.

This PR proposes to change the check to `lat2 - maxLatDelta >= latBase` in order to avoid the integer overflow.

part.text:
The fix is complete and validated. Summary:

**Root cause:** In `GeoEncodingUtils.Grid`-based predicates, the latitude bounds check `lat2 >= latBase + maxLatDelta` overflows `int` when the query shape touches the top of the latitude range: `latBase = 2147483646`, `maxLatDelta = 2` → `latBase + maxLatDelta` wraps to `-2147483648`, so the condition is always true and every point is rejected. This only bites at high latitudes because the longitude check already uses the overflow-safe form `lon2 - lonBase >= maxLonDelta`.

**Fix** (lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/geo/GeoEncodingUtils.java:366 and :414) — same as upstream apache/lucene#13704:
```java
if (lat2 < latBase || lat2 - latBase >= maxLatDelta) {
```
applied to both `DistancePredicate.test` and `Component2DPredicate.test`.

**Validation** (gradle suite can't run in the container — incomplete dist, no network — so I compiled `lucene/core` with javac and ran targeted harnesses):
- The exact `testNarrowPolygonCloseToNorthPole` scenario (doc-values predicate path and BKD cell-relate path) now matches, for both north and south pole mirrors.
- `DistancePredicate` self/far-point checks near both poles pass.
- A 1M-point fuzz comparing `predicate.test` to direct `Polygon2D.contains` shows behavior identical to baseline (only 8 pre-existing edge-quantization boundary cases, unchanged by this fix); full core compilation is clean, and no test files were modified.
